key_insight: CHARM introduces a multimodal graph foundation model that learns hierarchical context, enabling zero-shot transfer across graph domains without requiring task-specific labels or retraining. In simple terms, it aims to generalize graph understanding from text, images, and structure together.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the challenge of transferring graph models to new multimodal graph domains where labels are scarce or unavailable, and where standard methods struggle to leverage node modalities beyond graph topology.
method: Builds a multimodal graph foundation model that jointly encodes structure, text, images, and other node-level modalities.
Uses hierarchical context modeling to capture both local neighborhood signals and broader graph-level semantics.
Targets zero-shot transfer so the model can apply to unseen graph domains and tasks without fine-tuning on labeled data.
impact: This matters because many real-world graphs are multimodal and expensive to label, so a zero-shot model can dramatically reduce adaptation cost. For practitioners, CHARM points toward more scalable graph learning systems that generalize better across domains.
visual_elements: A pipeline diagram showing multimodal inputs flowing into CHARM and then transferring to unseen graph tasks.

paper_title: CHARM: A Multimodal Graph Foundation Model with Hierarchical Context Modeling for Zero-Shot Transfer
paper_authors: Ankang Yang, Jitao Zhao, Di Jin, Yuxiao Huang, Dongxiao He
